test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 01 Sept, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A 360 m long train running at the speed of 108 km/h crosses another train running in the opposite direction at the speed of 90 km/h in 12 seconds. What is the length (in m) of the other train?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative Speed in opposite direction = 108 + 90 = 198 km/h.

Speed in m/s = 198 × (5/18) = 55 m/s.

Total distance covered in 12 seconds = 55 × 12 = 660 m.

Length of the other train = Total distance − Length of first train.

Length = 660 − 360 = 300 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 300 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of train 1 (L₁) = 360 m

Speed of train 1 (S₁) = 108 km/h

Speed of train 2 (S₂) = 90 km/h

Time taken to cross (T) = 12 s

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = S₁ + S₂

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × (5/18)

Distance = Speed × Time

 
• 
• Train 1 
 108 km/h L1 = 360 m Train 2 
 90 km/h L2 = ? Opposite Direction Crossing Time = 12 s Total Distance = L1 + L2 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 108 + 90 = 198 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 198 × (5/18) = 55 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = L₁ + L₂ = 360 + L₂

⇒ Total Distance = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ 360 + L₂ = 55 × 12

⇒ 360 + L₂ = 660

⇒ L₂ = 660 − 360 = 300

**∴ The correct answer is 300 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects are moving in opposite directions towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). If they travel in the same direction, it is the difference (S₁ − S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply the value by 18/5.

Train Crossing Concept

When a train crosses another moving or stationary train, the total distance covered during the crossing is equal to the sum of the lengths of both trains (L₁ + L₂).
